uniequip_002_blaze2:
'D-Don't you go dismissing it as crude and simple just yet! There's a story behind it!
'Before I came to Rhodes Island, I moved back near my old home in Victoria for a spell. No one was really taking care of things there, and life was hard for the Infected. Back then, I was busy helping them fight for wages and medicine. I was also worried that my actions might cause my mum trouble. That's why I never went back to see her for years.
'I gave whatever medicine I could get my hands on to people who were sicker than I was. I felt like I could still walk around just fine, that I could hold out for a long time. But one day, without any warning, I just collapsed. My blood felt like it was boiling, my organs felt like porcelain about to crack from the heat...
'I'd imagined that, when I finally fell, I'd be unwilling to accept defeat, unable to let go of the workers I was helping. But when the moment actually came, and I was lying there alone in my shack... all I did was claw around for some scrap wood and carve a crude and tiny wooden lamp. I had no matches, so I lit it with a drop of my own blood, and then I just kept staring at it.
'I remembered how my mum used to light one of those lamps at the front door. Through all those years, we never moved, and she never stopped doing it. She said it was so when my dad finally came back, he could find his way home. Every time I went back home, that lamp was what stuck in my mind the most. And I was more surprised than anyone that, when I was about to die, that lamp was what I wanted to see most, more than anything. Somehow, though I failed to realize it at the time, staring at it eased my pain and dampened my symptoms... I was able to hold on until my companions found me.
'This lamp? No, this isn't that same broken old lamp—I made a new one. I'm no master craftsman, but you're not gonna turn up your nose at my creations, are you?'
When Ning Yin first heard Blaze tell her that story, all she felt was fear at the thought of what Blaze had been through. Next, when she thought about how Blaze had come all this way in the middle of the New Years holiday to bring her that lamp, a gift of such special significance, she forced a smile and praised the gift.
'No, that's not why I'm telling you all this... ah, listen to me, stumbling over my words again!' Blaze let her actions speak instead, hanging the lamp in Ning Yin's tiny apartment. Then she began briskly setting out the food and drink she'd brought. The smell of warm food slowly brought Ning Yin back to herself. It had been far too long since her little apartment had felt this lively. The lamp's soft, hand-crafted glow chased away every trace of loneliness.
'It's not the lamp that matters,' Blaze said quietly, 'but what it reminds you of, right?'
uniequip_003_blaze2:
“‘没事’，但并不是真的无事发生。可能只是对方不介意，又或者其实这个人很介意，但选择不说。不说可能是因为和你太熟，怕伤害你的感情。也可能是因为和你不熟，不想和你多费口舌。
“‘你看着办’，听起来是让你决定，但既可能是对方信任你的表现，也可能是一种漠视和嫌弃。如果是前者，那么其实你最终还是要以说这句话的人的意见为准，以此来表示感激和尊敬。如果是后者，那就更复杂了，你不光不能真的擅作主张，还得想清楚自己因为什么事而得罪了对方——
“这真的太费脑子了！
“和那些人比起来，沙漠里那种一生只叫一次的洞穴鼷兽都显得啰嗦了！”
煌一把捏断了手中的笔，墨水溅了一身。她长叹一口气，在客房里翻找半天，也只找出了惊蛰为她准备的那一身天师风格的装束。
“都怪麟青砚，事先不提醒我，害我在街上出丑不说，现在连和人沟通的小抄都得我自己写！”想到前两天在百灶大街上那一幕幕，煌不禁扶额长叹。
“下次看见几个人在饭馆柜台前争吵推搡，我再也不会去把他们扭送到大理寺了！
“下次有服务员笑眯眯问我茶泡得没味儿了要不要换一壶，我再也不会说‘好的’然后一直待到他们打烊了！
“有什么话不能直说吗？！”煌越想越气，干脆把那张小抄连同笔记本一起扔到了客房角落里。
……
顾烛煌回到客房，最后检查了一遍行李，明天她就要离开百灶了。角落里被窗帘盖住的一个笔记本引起了她的注意。她捡了起来，想起了自己刚到百灶时的样子。
“有什么话不能直说吗……”顾烛煌认真地想了想，“还真有。”
她干脆从行李箱里找出笔，接着那张小纸条的最后一句，给当初的自己写了几句回信。
“煌，在进入炎国这个陌生的故乡时，你难以避免地感到了担忧和害怕。但当你不再害怕，把自己真的当成这里的人之后，就会发现，其实直来直去也没问题。直率和勇气，在炎国同样是好的品质。
“况且，有时候那些没说出口的话，反而更让人刻骨铭心。”
